documents.language:
# Oathkeeper 0.1 language and semantics

## Declarations

```text
module dotted.name;
use package.module.Name;
use package.module.{Name, Other as Alias};
type Record<T> = { field: T, other: Bool };
type Alias = Int;
enum Option<T> { None, Some(T) }
const named_value [: Type] = expression;
fn function<T>(argument: T) -> T { argument }
query question(argument: Type) -> Answer {
    scope = boolean_expression;
    applies = boolean_expression;
    meta = typed_constant;
}
rule named_rule for question(argument) {
    when = boolean_expression;
    yield = expression;
    meta = typed_constant;
}
priority named_priority for question(argument) {
    higher = named_rule;
    lower = another_rule;
    when = boolean_expression;
    meta = typed_constant;
}
```

The `meta` field is optional on queries, rules and priorities. Other legal
annotations are ordinary typed constants referencing the relevant symbol or
source. No legal source category is a reserved declaration keyword.

Identifiers are ASCII letters/underscore followed by letters/digits/underscore.
Names are case-sensitive. Modules are explicitly imported. All declarations in
the entry's transitive import closure participate, including rules not reachable
by expression calls. There is no discovery from directory proximity. The locked
source snapshot is parsed and the included closure is typechecked; syntax errors
anywhere in the snapshot are diagnosed. Mutually importing modules are allowed;
executable dependencies must remain acyclic.

Declarations are globally identified by module and name. Fully qualified
references still require the declaration's module to be in the import closure.
Duplicate declarations, import aliases, fields, parameters and priority cycles
are errors. Cycles of legal IDs in data do not constitute executable recursion.

## Types and expressions

Kernel types are `Unit`, `Bool`, `Text`, `Int`, `Rational`, finite
`List<T>`, nominal records and nominal variants. Function declarations are
statically resolved; function values, closures, partial application and dynamic
dispatch are not available in v0.1.

Type parameters are inferred from arguments and context. Explicit arguments use
`Box::<Int> { value: 1 }`, `Option.None::<Int>()` where a contextual type is
unavailable, or `function::<Int>(1)`. Prefer a type annotation for an empty
list or payload-free generic variant. Record fields must exactly match the
declared schema. Currencies use nominal phantom parameters, e.g. `Money<USD>`.

Expressions include literals, record/variant construction, field access, calls,
`if condition { yes } else { no }`, exhaustive `match`, and block bindings:

```oath
fn twice(x: Int) -> Int { x * 2 }
fn total(acc: Int, x: Int) -> Int { acc + x }
fn example() -> Int {
    let values = map([1, 2, 3], twice);
    fold(values, 0, total)
}
```

`map`, `filter`, `fold`, `all` and `any` accept named, statically resolved
functions. All traversal follows list order. `all` and `any` stop on a decisive
value. A missing filter predicate prevents a known filtered list.

Operator precedence, from weakest to strongest: `or`; `and`;
`== !=`; `< <= > >=`; `+ -`; `* / %`; unary `- not !`;
calls and field access. Division produces Rational, even for Int operands.
Other arithmetic requires matching numeric types. Int literals can acquire a
Rational contextual type; arbitrary implicit conversions are absent.

Integer remainder follows truncation toward zero. The explicit
`floor_div(a,b)` primitive uses floor division. Decimal literals are exact
fractions; all wire rationals are reduced with positive denominators.
Division by zero, invalid indexing and `fail(message)` are execution errors,
not query outcomes. Conditions are Bool, not arbitrary truthy values.

Primitive functions are:
`len, at, append, concat, range, to_rational, floor, floor_div, text_len,
text_at, parse_int, int_text, fail`.
`range(start,end)` is half-open, ascending and empty when end <= start.
Text indexing counts Unicode scalar values, not UTF-8 bytes or graphemes.
No locale-dependent ordering is used.

Ordering is structural and deterministic: numeric order, Unicode scalar text
order, field-name order for records, variant-name then payload order for enums,
and lexicographic list order. Compared values must have the same static type.
Set/map constructors in std.collections normalize entries to this order.
Public record construction can bypass these library invariants; use the
normalizing functions for values claimed to be sets/maps.

## Knowledge and outcomes

Every scenario field is Known, Missing, or Disputed. A known record may contain
missing fields; accessing a different known field remains possible. Known false,
known None, missing Option, and a known empty list are distinct. A list does not
assert that its real-world inventory is complete.

Agreeing disputed claims combine evidence. Differing claims remain disputed.
Evidence IDs are supplied labels, not authenticated facts. The evaluator
propagates blockers through relevant operations; it does not assume negation
when proof is absent.

`false and unknown` and `unknown and false` are false.
`true or unknown` and `unknown or true` are true. Left-to-right short circuit
avoids evaluating the right operand when the left decides the result. An unknown
conditional does not select either branch, even if its branches look equal.

Query evaluation:

1. False scope -> OutsideCoverage; unresolved scope -> Undetermined.
2. False applicability -> Inapplicable; unresolved applicability -> Undetermined.
3. Evaluate every included candidate guard and every priority condition.
4. Any unresolved guard/priority -> Undetermined in v0.1.
5. Compute maximal active rules using enabled priority's transitive closure.
6. Evaluate only maximal yields. Missing yielded data -> Undetermined.
7. Equal normalized answers combine support. Different answers -> Conflicted.
8. No active rule -> Undetermined with NoSupportingRule.

Priority is a strict partial order, scoped to one query. Its transitive relation
passes through inactive intermediate rules. All potential cycles are rejected,
even if conditions appear mutually exclusive. Source order, directory depth,
source dates, and source citations confer no priority.

Consuming an unresolved query propagates issues. Consuming an inapplicable,
unsupported or conflicted query produces a named dependency issue, never false,
zero or an empty list. Resolved false remains false.

Independent obligations should be explicitly collected, with an authored empty
collection for no contributions. They should not be encoded as incompatible
answers to a single-valued query.

## Calendars and effects

`std.date.Date` is a nominal record containing a civil-day index relative to
1970-01-01, using the proleptic Gregorian calendar and astronomical year numbering.
Its constructors return Result for invalid dates; `date` is a checked convenience
that raises an error. ISO parsing accepts exactly YYYY-MM-DD, including year 0000.
`add_months` requires Reject or Clamp overflow policy. Dates are not instants.

`std.numeric.round` takes an explicit positive quantum and mode. No money or
calendar operation reads the clock. Currency conversion requires an explicit
rate. Domain deadlines, enactment, commencement, savings clauses, authority
cutoffs and transitions are ordinary authored functions/queries in lawlib.

Execution does not cause legal or institutional acts. An event must be supplied
as input to an authored pure state transition.
documents.formats:
# Packages, requests, results and CLI

## Package snapshot

`oath.toml` declares package identity, exact language version, entry under
`src/`, and local dependencies with exact versions. `oath lock PACKAGE`
explicitly creates/updates `oath.lock`. All other commands require the lock to
match the resolved snapshot and never rewrite it. Dependencies are local paths;
there is no registry, network package resolution or implicit latest selection.

Digests include normalized manifest information, all authored `src/**/*.oath`
paths/bytes and dependency digests. Dependency paths are resolution hints and are
excluded from identity. CRLF is normalized to LF. Symlinked source entries are
rejected. Source references are ordinary constants inside hashed source files.
Scenario fixtures, original documents, caches, build products and absolute
checkout locations are excluded from program/package identity.

The compiled program digest additionally binds typed IR, source spans,
included-module inventory and semantics version. Changing source formatting can
change a digest even if a legal answer is unchanged.

## JSON protocol

Generated schemas are in [schemas/v0.1](../schemas/v0.1). Regenerate with:

```sh
cargo run -p oathkeeper --example export_schemas
```

Schemas describe structure; the typed reader additionally checks canonical
numbers, nominal types, arity, limits, duplicate keys, reference integrity and
semantics versions. The manifest schema describes the TOML data model in JSON.

A request identifies exactly one root query and exactly its named arguments.
Unknown arguments must be present as Missing observations:

```json
{
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "query": "demo.noise_status",
  "arguments": {
    "emergency": {
      "state": "known",
      "value": {"type": "bool", "value": true},
      "evidence": ["finding:emergency.1"]
    }
  },
  "metadata": {}
}
```

Metadata is a string-to-string extension map and does not participate in legal
conditions. Findings, interpretation profiles, cutoff dates and completeness
assertions used by a program belong in typed arguments. They are bound by the
request digest.

Int uses `{"type":"int","value":"7000"}`; Rational uses
`{"type":"rational","numerator":"7","denominator":"100"}`.
Records use `name`, `type_args`, and observation-valued `fields`; variants
also identify their `variant` and ordered observation-valued payload fields.
Generic type arguments use the schema's `Ty` representation.

All object keys are unique, unknown semantic fields are rejected, and integer
strings have no leading zeros, plus sign, exponent or negative zero. JSON numeric
tokens are only for safe-integer protocol counters; exact application numbers
are strings. Canonical encoding uses RFC 8785 UTF-16 key order and its integer-only
subset, with SHA-256 domain prefixes `oathkeeper:DOMAIN:v1\0`. Application
values are normalized before result comparison and certificate emission.

Each result has one outcome, rule support, used premise IDs, metadata references,
and the included closure's declared coverage references. These coverage records
are declarations, not a claim that every entry applies to the root query.
The certificate's postorder trace is the explanation graph; it is not duplicated
in a second graph field. Nodes identify expression spans, input environments,
calculations, branches, dependencies and complete rule/priority inventories.

## Commands

```text
oath run PACKAGE --request FILE --format text|json --certificate FILE [--limits FILE]
oath test PACKAGE [--json]
oath verify PACKAGE --request FILE --certificate FILE [--limits FILE] [--format text|json]
oath lock PACKAGE
oath check PACKAGE
oath coverage PACKAGE [--json]
oath sources check PACKAGE [--fetch] [--cache DIRECTORY]
```

The certificate option is optional for run; the Rust API always returns one.
JSON run output is the QueryResult; the separate certificate file contains
the result and derivation. Verify receives the caller's locked package and
request and cannot let a certificate select either.

Fixture JSON files under `tests/` contain `name`, `request`, `expected` and
optional `limits`. Expectations choose either an operational error or an
outcome with optional value/stage/issue/support assertions. The harness calls the
same run API and then independently verifies every successful derivation,
including unresolved and conflicted outcomes.

Source auditing reads optional cache entries named by raw-byte SHA-256 or
`fixture:relative/path` references. Only `--fetch` permits HTTPS retrieval.
Matched, Mismatched and Unavailable are audit results; NotChecked is reserved for
records not submitted to auditing. Run and computational verify never read these
documents. A missing archive can therefore prevent an audit without changing an
answer or certificate.

## Resource profile

Defaults: 1,000,000 evaluated expressions/query entries, 250,000 trace nodes,
100,000 collection entries, call depth 128, 65,536 bits per exact component,
64 MiB per input/certificate and JSON nesting 128.

An execution-limit file contains the complete ExecutionLimits object. Verification
requires the same profile as the certificate. A successful trace contains one
node per evaluation step. The checker separately enforces its own work bound.
Overflowing any bound is operational failure, never a legal answer.

v0.1 permits configuring work/size budgets but fixes safety ceilings of 128 for
call depth and nesting. Depth counts expression evaluation as well as function
and query calls. Compiler expression/type nesting is also bounded. Workers
reserve a 32 MiB stack so host thread defaults do not change these guarantees.
Limits bound logical work and stored structures; they are not a hard process
RSS cap or a wall-clock timeout. Deploy hostile workloads with process isolation.
documents.verification:
# What verification establishes

Computational verification means the recorded answer follows from the
caller-supplied compiled program and scenario, under the recorded semantics and
limits. Source-byte integrity and legal review are separate assurances.

`oath-verify` depends only on `oath-core`. It does not depend on or call
`oathkeeper`, its interpreter, package loader or source fetcher. The interpreter
uses graph reachability to select rules; the checker independently reconstructs
the complete rule inventory and uses topological closure. Core shares values,
primitive arithmetic, observation operations, pattern binding, wire encoding and
structural IR checks, but no rule-selection procedure.

The checker validates every consumed node against the expected expression and
environment, checks branches and arithmetic, checks all candidates and priority
conditions, reconstructs the outcome and provenance, and rejects missing, extra,
reused, cyclic or out-of-bounds trace references. The program, package, request,
limits and result are bound by domain-separated digests.

The trusted computing base includes the source-to-IR compiler, structural IR
validator, checker, exact-number implementation, serializers, hash implementation,
Rust/toolchain/runtime and platform. Compilation is not formally proved.
Structural validation rejects malformed references but is not a replacement for
the compiler's full type and dependency analysis. Public APIs expect a program
produced by compile; deserialized arbitrary IR is not a trusted program.

Calendar, monetary and legal functions in `.oath` are visible computations,
checked through the same derivations. Their algorithms and interpretations still
need tests and review. There is no hidden trusted tax or calendar oracle.

Evidence names, purported judges, completeness assertions and selected readings
are premises. They are not authenticated by their labels. Used-premise reporting
is conservative: reading a containing record can include evidence attached to its
other fields. It is not a proof of a minimal premise set.

SourceRef hashes bind the original document bytes, not legal authority or faithful
translation. HTML changes can invalidate an audit without changing underlying
law. A URL and hash do not recover a lost historical version. ReviewStatus records
a review assertion; v0.1 does not implement signatures, reviewer identity
authentication or a credential system.

Coverage records expose investigated sources, exclusions, uninvestigated areas
and unresolved interpretations. Successful checks do not demonstrate that no
other source or rule is relevant.
documents.release:
# 0.1.0 developer release

The initial implementation includes the four-crate workspace, functional
compiler/interpreter, independent checker, standard library, local packages and
locks, CLI/API, schemas, conformance/adversarial/property tests, fuzz targets and
separate lawlib integration.

No remote repositories have been created or published. The supplied Git
repositories are local and independent. Hosted workflows are configured but
must run in the user's eventual hosting environment.

## Pinning and CI

Oathkeeper builds and tests without lawlib. Its optional integration job uses
`integration/lawlib.json`, an exact lawlib commit. Set the repository variable
`LAWLIB_REPOSITORY` to the eventual owner/repository to enable that job.

Lawlib's `compatibility.json` pins an exact Oathkeeper candidate commit. A
subsequent Oathkeeper integration-pin commit changes no runtime code, avoiding a
circular moving-branch dependency. Lawlib CI requires its
`OATHKEEPER_REPOSITORY` variable. Existing content locks pin the std snapshot.

Each repository has an independent version/release history. Release snapshots
should remain immutable. For an amendment or encoding correction, update source
and rationale, keep historical revisions, add fixtures, explicitly relock affected
packages, and make a new release.

## Verification

The test suite includes independently authored expected outcomes, evaluator/checker
agreement, forged and omitted certificate premises, malformed traces, exact
arithmetic properties, calendar/rounding boundaries, portability and bounded
parser/reader mutation. Lawlib has separate scenario fixtures; each successful
run is independently checked. Source audits are separate from deterministic tests.

Native Windows GNU and WSL Linux are the local validation targets. The CI matrix
also describes Windows MSVC and hosted Ubuntu. Local GNU success does not claim
that hosted MSVC CI has already run. See the generated initial
`VALIDATION.md` for actual completed checks.

## Deliberate v0.1 limits

- Interpreted typed IR, no optimizer/native backend, recursion or dynamic dispatch.
- Single-root requests and conservative blocking on every unknown candidate guard
  or priority. No universal legal decision procedure.
- Local dependency resolution; external archives and authenticated review/signature
  infrastructure are not implemented.
- JSON schemas describe wire shape; reader/typechecker enforce semantic invariants.
- Source metadata validation recognizes the standard SourceRef/SourceAnchor schemas;
  arbitrary private legal ID graphs still require authored validation/review.
- Source-to-IR correctness is tested, not formally proved. The checker is independent
  implementation, not a theorem-prover kernel.
- Trace graphs are deliberately explicit and can be large. Resource errors can
  occur before nominal collection limits due to certificate-size constraints.
- Metadata attaches directly to queries/rules/priorities. Other declarations use
  ordinary provenance constants and explicit symbol references.

The expansion chapter of the accepted plan is an ongoing roadmap. General legal
impact analysis, full historical authority discovery and comprehensive legal
coverage are not delivered by these initial examples.

# Coverage matrix — initial developer snapshot

All rows are **Unreviewed** legally. Source integrity is a separate, time-specific
audit; rerun `sources check` against the referenced bytes. No table cell claims
exhaustive discovery of relevant law.

| Area | Representation | Executable example | Unresolved/uninvestigated work |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sources and history | SourceRef, anchors, instrument/revision/lifecycle/link records | Household amendment; delayed commencement | Comprehensive historical archives and amendment ingestion |
| Institutions and authority | Institutions, contextual relationships, powers | Narrow federal authority profiles | Full federal/state/tribal/local competences and conflicts |
| Lawmaking | Event/lifecycle/power records | Amendment XX; supplied institutional transition | Full legislative and administrative procedures |
| Rights and duties | Right, Obligation, Act, LegalEffect | Quiet hours and notice deadline | General rights/liability doctrine |
| Interpretation | Issues, findings, interpretation and proposition records | Thornton classification; synthetic conflicting readings | Automated analogy or holding extraction is outside v0.1 |
| Evidence | EvidenceRecord, Finding, ProofStandard | Missing/disputed/accepted emergency findings | Admissibility, burdens and authentic decision-maker authority |
| Procedure | Proceedings, stages, events and pure transitions | Notice delivery and calendar deadline function | Litigation and agency procedure |
| Adjudication | Case, Opinion, Judgment | Thornton source mapping | Full adjudication, jurisdiction and preclusion |
| Appeals and treatment | Proposition/opinion/judgment-specific Treatment | Synthetic targeted overruling and unaffected proposition | Actual citator coverage and appeal histories |
| Enforcement | Consequence and power data | No automatic fine from violation | Real enforcement mechanisms |
| Remedies | Separate consequence queries | Explicit absence of supporting fine rule | Remedy eligibility, measure and enforcement |
| Constitutional text | All 7 Articles and 27 Amendments mapped | Selected requirements, thresholds and commencement | Most constitutional doctrine and provisions |
| Tax calculations | Exact amounts, inventory completeness and explicit rounding | Constrained 2025 IRA allocation | Other tax years, transactions, taxes and comprehensive authority review |

Known exclusions are named in each package's CoverageRecord. The
`not_investigated` fields identify areas without a completeness claim. Model
availability is representation support, not executable legal coverage.
documents.encoding:
# Encoding conventions

Use nominal records and explicit functions/queries for legal concepts. Sources,
instruments, provisions, revisions, cases, opinions, judgments, propositions,
treatments, findings, rights, duties, powers and proceedings are library data.
There is no universal legal rank, implicit retroactivity or automatic preemption.

An encoding record links a rule to source anchors, interpretation rationale,
assumptions and a review status. A citation does not activate an authority.
Use scope and applicability expressions to describe the encoded effect and
conditional priority declarations to resolve authored exceptions.

Treat provision identity, source-document identity, locator, revision identity
and encoding release as separate concepts. Keep old revisions. A saved earlier
event can remain governed by an older rule after an amendment. Separate adoption,
enactment, commencement, applicability, expiration and historical-authority
cutoffs; the engine has no implicit current date.

Findings and evidence remain supplied premises. Keep competing claims even
when selecting an accepted interpretation. Record the issue, decision-maker,
role, scope, evidence, rationale and supersession explicitly. A role label
does not authenticate competence or adjudication. Burdens, admissibility and
review standards require their own legal rules; do not replace them with
invented probabilities.

Precedent modeling separates litigation, reasoning, disposition, interpreted
propositions and later treatment. A treatment targets the relevant proposition,
opinion or judgment, with context and temporal reach. No whole-case valid flag
stands in for this analysis.

The initial authority package supports majority holdings in the two named
federal profiles and distinguishes concurrence/dissent. Per curiam, fractured,
en banc/panel precedence, Erie questions and unsupported forums require further
encoding. Citation permission and persuasive relevance are supplied analyses,
not inferred from publication alone. Unknown findings remain observations.

The Constitution package evaluates specified textual requirements, not overall
eligibility. Its voting queries answer numeric threshold questions only; they
do not decide quorum, valid votes, procedure or every Article V condition.
Amendment XX sections 1-2 commence on 1933-10-15; the separate section-4 example
uses ratification on 1933-01-23. Sources: [National Archives](https://www.archives.gov/founding-docs/amendments-11-27).
The Thornton query requires accepted classification and authority findings and
only addresses an additional state qualification for congressional service.

The IRA model uses the identified 2024 codification of sections 219, 408 and 408A,
reconciled to the dated 2025 Form 8606, its instructions and Notice 2024-80.
It does not claim an exhaustive 2025 legislative or precedent review.
Do not relabel the statutory source edition as 2025.

Contribution queries support a supplied aggregate of other personal IRA
contributions for the annual cap. Conversion allocation deliberately requires
that other aggregate to be zero, so no unmodeled current-year basis is omitted.
The conversion profile includes complete, uniquely identified relevant own
traditional/SEP/SIMPLE accounts, complete basis/transaction histories, qualifying
compensation and a nondeductible designation. It excludes inherited accounts,
RMDs, corrections, outstanding rollovers, other distributions, cross-year
transactions, special transactions, deduction phaseouts and state tax.

Exact taxable allocation and reporting projection are separate queries. The
projection uses six fractional decimal places at line 10, then the caller's
positive output quantum with HalfAwayFromZero. It is an explicit policy within
the form's at-least-three-place instruction, not a universal rounding rule.
See [2025 Form 8606](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f8606--2025.pdf) and
[instructions](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i8606--2025.pdf).

Legal consequences need authored rules. A prohibition does not automatically
create liability, invalidity, enforcement authority, damages or a remedy.
Compatible effects should be accumulated explicitly. A pure state-transition
function records the modeled consequences of supplied events; it performs no
governmental or private act.

Before expanding coverage, add positive, negative, boundary, missing-fact,
disputed-interpretation and temporal fixtures. Record both reviewed exclusions
and questions never investigated. Maintain independent expected answers in
fixtures; evaluator/checker agreement alone cannot establish domain correctness.
